newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Strong oil price to boost BP profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Strong oil price to boost BP profit.

text.p: Continued strength in oil prices will have been the main motor behind a healthy fourth quarter and full year profit rise for British Petroleum, analysts said on Friday.
BP is due to announce results on February 11.
Higher oil and gas production and a better performance in chemicals would also help results, along with a slight improvement in refining, they added.
"It is going to be good all round," said analyst Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.

Forecasts for net profit before exceptional items range between 2.50 and 2.75 billion stg, compared with 2.01 billion a year ago. The forecasts are for results on a replacement cost basis, which strip out windfall profits or losses resulting from fluctuations in oil and chemical stock prices.
The dividend payout is expected to rise sharply to between 19.25 and 19.80 pence from 15.25 pence.

Oil companies across the world were helped last year by a surprisingly high oil price, which averaged just over $20 per barrel. This contrasted sharply with market expectations at the start of 1996, when consensus was for a level of just under $17.
But many analysts believe crude prices may retreat later in the year as non-Opec production picks up amid higher stock levels.
Refining margins may improve slightly, like the chemicals results but overall trading conditions for the oil majors are likely to be less favourable this year than last.

BP shares, however, are still favoured by most industry watchers, who praise the company for its persistent drive to cut costs. Additionally, analysts point to BP's low valuation compared with other integrated oil firms as a reason for liking the company's shares.
BP shares are currently trading at a prospective price-to- earnings ratio of 15.85, compared with a P/E of 17.65 for Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc, according to Reuters 3000.
"We still see BP as one of the best value stocks in the sector," broker Salomon Brothers wrote in a recent report on Shell and BP.
